question: A paediatric cardiologist refers a 4-month-old infant for surgical assessment. The child is cyanosed and a chest radiograph shows a boot-shaped heart (coeur en sabot). Which congenital heart disease is most likely, and what are the four anatomical components of this defect?

answers.text: Tetralogy of Fallot — VSD, pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, and overriding aorta

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The boot-shaped heart on X-ray (due to an upturned cardiac apex from RVH) with cyanosis is classic Tetralogy of Fallot. Its four components are VSD + pulmonary stenosis + RVH + overriding aorta — remembered as the 4 T's (Tetralogy of Fallot).

answers.text: Transposition of the great arteries — aorta arising from the right ventricle and pulmonary artery from the left

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Transposition of the great arteries causes cyanosis and an egg-on-side radiographic appearance — not a boot-shaped heart. It is one cyanotic defect but not the four-component Tetralogy.

answers.text: Ventricular septal defect — a deficiency in the interventricular septum with left-to-right shunting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. An uncomplicated VSD causes left-to-right shunting and is ACYANOTIC. Cyanosis in a VSD occurs only when shunt reversal develops (Eisenmenger syndrome) — a late complication, not a presentation in infancy.

answers.text: Atrial septal defect — a communication between the two atria with predominantly left-to-right shunting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ASD is an acyanotic lesion with left-to-right shunting and does not cause cyanosis in infancy. It also does not produce a boot-shaped heart on X-ray.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 4 T's of cyanotic congenital heart disease include Tetralogy of Fallot — its boot-shaped heart and four anatomical components (VSD, PS, RVH, overriding aorta) are high-yield surgical anatomy.
Well done. Boot-shaped heart + cyanosis = Tetralogy of Fallot. Remember all four components: VSD, pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, and overriding aorta.
